title: The Power of Words
summary: Practise Spanish synonyms and antonyms to improve your writing and understand what you read.
keyIdeas: Synonyms have the same or very similar meanings in a particular context.
Using suitable synonyms helps avoid repetition and improves writing.

basicKnowledge: D. Reflexión sobre la lengua y sus usos en el marco de propuestas de producción y comprensión de textos orales, escritos o multimodales

activities.prompt: Two words are synonyms if their meanings are opposite.
activities.explanation: False. Words with opposite meanings are antonyms. Synonyms have the same or very similar meanings.

activities.prompt: Match each Spanish word with its synonym.
activities.explanation: These pairs have similar meanings: «veloz/rápido», «comenzar/empezar», «alegre/contento» and «conversar/hablar».

activities.prompt: At school lunch, Hugo says the soup is «muy caliente». Which Spanish word expresses the opposite temperature?
activities.explanation: «Fría» is the opposite of «caliente» when describing temperature.
activities.hint: Choose the word with the opposite meaning to «caliente».

activities.prompt: Sort these Spanish word pairs by their relationship.
activities.explanation: Similar meanings make a synonym pair; opposite meanings make an antonym pair.

activities.prompt: Read the Spanish story about the park and answer the questions.
activities.explanation: Notice related and contrasting meanings to understand the characters' feelings and actions.
activities.title: El rescate del gatito
activities.text: Ayer por la tarde, Lucía y Martín paseaban por el parque municipal. De pronto, escucharon un maullido débil entre las ramas de un árbol frondoso. Un pequeño gato negro parecía asustado y no se atrevía a descender. Lucía buscó ayuda rápidamente y avisó a la jardinera del parque. Con una escalera alta y mucha paciencia, la mujer logró alcanzarlo. El felino, que antes temblaba de miedo, se mostró aliviado y comenzó a ronronear con calma. Los dos amigos regresaron a su casa muy contentos por haber ayudado al animal.

questions.prompt: Which word in the text means the same as «bajar»?
questions.explanation: Here, «descender» and «bajar» both mean to move from a higher place to a lower one.

questions.prompt: Which word describes the cat's initial feeling that contrasts with «aliviado» at the end?
questions.explanation: In this story, «asustado» contrasts with «aliviado»: the cat goes from fear to calm.

activities.prompt: Choose the Spanish word with a similar meaning to avoid repetition.
activities.explanation: Here, «fascinante» fits a positive description similar to «emocionante».
activities.sentence: Aisha leyó un cuento emocionante y después escribió un relato igual de ___.

activities.prompt: Nerea writes Spanish antonym pairs, but makes a mistake. Which pair is NOT a pair of antonyms?
activities.explanation: «Antiguo» and «viejo» can have similar meanings, so they do not form an opposite pair.
activities.hint: Find the pair with similar rather than opposite meanings.

activities.prompt: Complete the Spanish sentence with the suitable antonym formed using a prefix.
activities.explanation: «Injusto» is the opposite of «justo», formed with the prefix «in-».
activities.sentence: Tratar a una compañera peor que a los demás sin motivo es ___.

activities.prompt: Omar writes: «El examen de música fue muy duro». Which Spanish synonym best fits «duro» here?
activities.explanation: For a school test, «duro» means difficult, rather than physically hard or solid.
activities.hint: Think about the meaning of «duro» when describing a school test.

activities.prompt: Put these Spanish adjectives in order from smallest to largest in meaning.
